A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reaction of 2- and 4-aminomethyl quinolizidine derivatives with carbon dioxide leads to the formation of crystalline carbamates, which are stable at room temperature and in solution for several months.
we were able to stabilize aminomethylquinoline derivatives by forming carbamates.
the C5 substituents of 2- aminomethyl-quinoline derivatives influence the basicity and polarity of these compounds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 2-aminopropyl substituents of QCI and of QCD are more basic than the 2- aminomethyl substituents of the same compounds, but that the 2-aminoethyl substituents are less basic than the 3-aminoprop-1-yl substituents.
the 1,2-diamino derivatives of quinocorine and quincoridines can be stabilized in the solid state as crystalline ammonium carbamtes.
we can use the reaction of aminomethyl-substituted QCI and QCI with isatoic acid to synthesize the corresponding anthranilic amides 4-9.
